android.desc:
Network Cell Info Lite is a mobile network and WiFi analyzer for checking cellular signal strength, WiFi signal, cell info, and mobile network information in near real time. Diagnose bad reception, dropped calls, weak data connections, and coverage gaps on 5G, LTE+, LTE, IWLAN, UMTS, GSM, and CDMA networks.

Use Network Cell Info Lite to understand your phone signal and find better connectivity wherever you are. See the cell your phone is connected to, monitor cellular signal strength and mobile network signal strength, review signal history, and map your network’s real-world performance.

WiFi analyzer and internet speed test

• Use the WiFi analyzer to check WiFi signal quality and identify a stronger connection.
• Turn your device into a WiFi signal strength meter with clear WiFi and cellular gauges.
• Run a one-tap internet speed test for download speed, upload speed, ping, and jitter.
• View WiFi, cellular signal, and phone signal strength in almost real time with one-second monitoring.

Cellular signal meter and network diagnostics

• Monitor cellular signal strength, phone signal strength, and mobile network signal strength in Gauge and Raw views.
• See detailed mobile network info, including network type, serving cell information, and connection statistics for 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G.
• Use dual-SIM support with two or three cellular signal strength meters plus WiFi gauges.
• View network information conveniently in the status bar and export measurement history to your database.

Mobile coverage maps and signal history

• Explore a mobile coverage map with cellular network information and signal-meter gauges.
• Use Personal Best Signal Finder to review your signal strength history by location and find where you have had good reception.
• Use the crowdsourced Best Signal Finder to locate nearby areas with stronger signals for your carrier.
• Review signal plots for up to two cells and detailed history logs to understand changes in cellular signal and phone coverage over time.
• View cell-location indications on the map through Mozilla Location Service. These are location estimates, not physical carrier cell tower locations.

Bad Signal Reporter

Tired of bad phone reception or dead zones? With your opt-in, the Bad Signal Reporter records poor connectivity, including no signal and fringe coverage. These aggregated Bad Signal Reports are provided free to mobile network operators worldwide to help identify opportunities to improv

quotes.text:
I use Network Cell Info Lite[0] for this purpose.

Sadly, it's only available in the Google/Apple stores (if anyone knows of a similar tool that's available elsewhere, I'd love to hear about it!)

It allows me to locate the "cell towers" I'm connecting to and that are nearby, as well as the devices around me, and will map them for me.

In fact, several years ago, I noted a brand spanking new "cell tower a block or so away (this is in NYC) that appeared to be in the street(!).  It stayed there for a couple weeks and then was gone.  It sure seemed like it was an IMSI catcher[1].

It's not directly the feature set you suggest, but can certainly be used to identify the towers near you -- and any new ones that might "pop up."

[0] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.wilysis.cellinfolite&hl=en-US

[1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMSI-catcher

Edit: Another comment (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45189302 ) mentioned snoopsnitch (https://github.com/srlabs/snoopsnitch ) and other tools which, apparently can do similar (and more apropos to the topic at hand) things as Network Cell Info Lite.
